doc.title: Yusef Lateef — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Defining the music and its reception
title: Afro-Cuban and Latin jazz
summary: He has never led an Afro-Cuban group; the nearest was Gillespie's band and sessions with Ray Barretto and Olatunji.

story.theme_name: Playing with Coltrane and the avant-garde

blocks.x: Now, this is something that we, we touched upon to some degree when, when we were discussing uh, excuse me, your, your work with the Dizzy Gillespie Big Band, but if you could a bit more about your uh working with, for wont of a better word, with latin-jazz, or jazz with an afro-cuban influence.
Sorry, I used that word, didn’t I, “jazz?” Sorry, Mom. Okay. Yeah.
I’ve never worked with an afro-cuban group.
So, I guess, the Gillespie Orchestra would be the extent of, of that kind of flavor in, in, in your uh–
I suppose, although I’ve recorded with [Puerto Rican percussionist] Ray Barretto...
And um...[American percussionist] Chief Bey with the–
Yeah. That’s as close as I’ve gotten to that.
